lens: Layout and typography within the existing dark, compact account section. All 14 screenshots inspected. Responsive/accessibility scores cover visible readability and wrapping only; no keyboard, contrast-measurement, or outer-padding claims.

findings: Before layout 8: warning percentages sit far from their labels across the wide columns. Group each warning value with its label; the after screenshot resolves this.

Before content 7: 'Low' understates 0% remaining, and 'loaded / eligible' does not explicitly describe quota freshness. Use 'Exhausted', 'left', and a quota-current count; these improvements are visible after.
After hierarchy 8, down from 9: account names lose their bold weight while weekly percentages remain bold, weakening the identity anchor above each warning. Restore semibold account names.
Before content 7: replace 'Low' at 0% with 'Exhausted' and clarify remaining values and quota freshness. The after copy addresses these points.
After hierarchy 8, down from 9: regular-weight account names no longer clearly lead the secondary warning text. Restore semibold names.

After layout 7 and typography/numbers 8, down from 9: account 1 wraps 'Exhausted' onto a separate line while '0% left' remains beside the resource label. Put 'Exhausted · 0% left' together on a second line.

After consistency 8 and responsive/accessibility 8, down from 9: account 1 uses a detached right-aligned warning value while account 2 keeps 'Low 14% left' inline. Use the same label-then-status/value arrangement for both accounts at this width.
Before content 7: 'Low' at 0% and the generic loaded count obscure the specific condition. Use the after wording: 'Exhausted', remaining-value suffixes, and quotas current.
After hierarchy 8, down from 9: account names have the same regular weight as secondary labels, leaving percentages as the strongest row elements. Restore semibold names.

After layout 7 and typography/numbers 8, down from 9: the first warning gains a line, but its value stays on the preceding line. Group 'Exhausted · 0% left' beneath 'Cloud Session Credits' so the additional height buys a coherent reading order.
After consistency 8 and responsive/accessibility 8, down from 9: the first warning value is right-aligned while the second follows 'Low' inline. Apply a common compact warning layout to both rows.
Before content 7: the loaded count does not explain freshness, and 0% is described as merely 'Low'. The after quota-current count and 'Exhausted' label improve meaning.

After hierarchy 8, down from 9: the three-line credential name loses its stronger weight and blends more closely with the detail text below. Use semibold for the full account name while retaining the separate weekly-value column.

After layout 7 and typography/numbers 8, down from 9: the already tall first account gains a detached 'Exhausted' line, with '0% left' stranded above it. Put the status and value together beneath the resource label.

After consistency 8 and responsive/accessibility 8, down from 9: warning values switch between right-aligned and inline placement across adjacent accounts. Standardize their placement at this width; preserve the explicit 'Weekly quota unavailable' message.
Before layout 8: warning values sit apart from their labels. Keep each warning label, status, and value together, as shown after.
Before content 7: '2 loaded · 3 eligible' leaves the counted condition implicit, and 0% is labeled 'Low'. Use the after wording '2/3 quotas current' and 'Exhausted 0% left'.
After hierarchy 8, down from 9: account names lose emphasis relative to bold weekly values and amber warnings. Restore semibold names.
The unavailable account retains both its dash and explicit explanation; the improved header makes the partial state easier to understand.

Before hierarchy 8, typography/numbers 8, and controls/states 8: the stale 82.8% has the same bold emphasis as current values, while 'Stale' is unbounded inline text. De-emphasize the stale number and give its status a distinct treatment; both changes are visible after.
Before layout 8: warning percentages are detached from their resource labels. Group them inline, as shown after.
Before content 7: the header does not explicitly count current quotas, and 0% is labeled 'Low'. Adopt the after quota-current count and exhausted wording.
After hierarchy remains 8: the stale value is better differentiated, but account names have lost their previous emphasis. Restore semibold account names while retaining the subdued stale percentage.

Before content 7: bare detail percentages leave their direction implicit, 0% is labeled 'Low', and the header count is generic. The after 'left' suffixes, 'Exhausted' label, and quota-current count resolve these issues.
After hierarchy 8, down from 9: regular-weight account names sit beside similarly weighted plan metadata and above regular-weight detail labels. Restore semibold names to anchor each expanded column.

After controls/states 6 and consistency 6, down from 9: the Cloud Session Credits bar changes from an empty track before to an apparently full gray bar after despite reading 'Exhausted 0% left'. Restore zero visible fill for 0% remaining, using the same remaining-capacity direction as the other bars.
The repeated 'left' suffixes fit the expanded numeric columns without visible wrapping; the aligned detail rows and metadata groups remain readable.
